subject.title: Google Chat: agent-to-agent (bot↔bot) conversation doesn't work — a Chat app doesn't receive messages from another Chat app (same setup works on Discord)

question: Should this issue be resolved as a docs-only Google Chat limitation, or should OpenClaw design an opt-in channel-independent A2A bridge for addressed agent messages?
rationale: The docs fix is narrow and aligned with current behavior, but the bridge would intentionally change cross-agent/channel routing semantics and needs maintainer ownership before implementation.

options.title: Document caveat first
options.body: Add Google Chat and bot-loop/multi-agent docs that peer Chat-app messages may not produce inbound events, and point users to explicit `sessions_send`/A2A tooling for channel-independent agent messaging.

options.title: Design opt-in bridge
options.body: Keep the issue open for a generic bridge design that reuses `tools.agentToAgent` allowlists, loop limits, and live Google Chat proof before implementation.

options.title: Close as platform limitation
options.body: Decide not to support implicit bot-to-bot Google Chat conversations and close after documenting the unsupported platform behavior.

recommendation.title: Document caveat first
recommendation.body: Add Google Chat and bot-loop/multi-agent docs that peer Chat-app messages may not produce inbound events, and point users to explicit `sessions_send`/A2A tooling for channel-independent agent messaging.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans generic bot-loop protection, multi-agent routing, and product policy rather than only Google Chat parsing.
